chunks: Who can neither help them, nor help themselves?

key_terms.يَسْتَطِيعُونَ: can be able to / have the power to

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the inability of idols to help their worshippers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the ontological weakness of all created beings, whether idols or angels, emphasizing that they lack independent agency (istiqlal) and can only act by God's permission. It serves as a foundational argument against shirk, illustrating that false deities are merely servants like their worshippers, unable to offer salvation or even preserve their own existence. This reinforces the concept of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, where worship is due solely to the Self-Subsisting God.
